findings.meaning: Generic statement that personal pronouns exhibit case inflection; not the form mapping.

findings.statement: Bokmal nominative/accusative paradigm includes jeg/meg, du/deg, han/ham, hun/henne, den/den, det/det, vi/oss, dere/dere, de/dem.

conclusion: The specific form paradigm exists in source-backed grammar knowledge, but has no observed compiled grammar_rules row or rule-source link in Production. R079 correctly observed missing runtime case features but identified the generic classification entry rather than this specific runtime-intended paradigm as the closest source. The form mapping must be derived from this paradigm with provenance and tested bidirectionally; do not treat existing lexeme forms as the rule authority.
next_proof: Inspect compilation eligibility and manifest/binding contract for pronoun.personal.forms.bokmal.paradigm; produce case features in canonical tokens, test recognition and generation for jeg/meg, du/deg, hun/henne and ambiguous han, then retest subject selection without silently resolving noun-noun ambiguity.
